॥ Om, regarding the attainment of the inner Self. ॥ 1/2/13 ॥

It is said that Vishnu is in the Sun. In the passage beginning with “That person who is in the Sun, I am that; that very one I am,” the position of the Agnis (fires) in the Sun and other deities is stated. Therefore, due to the identity of the Sun and the eye, in the passage “That person who is seen in the eye,” it is the Agni (fire) itself that is referred to. Hence, from the knowledge of Agni, liberation from the attachment of all sins is attained, as in the passage: “Just as water does not cling to the lotus leaf or the water-lily leaf, so for one who knows this, sinful actions do not cling.” Therefore, he said: “Regarding the attainment of the inner Self.” The Vishnu residing within the eye is the same. This is established by the passage beginning with “Three parts of the immortal are in the heaven,” which establishes his immortality and so on. It is also established by the word “Brahman.” The passage beginning with “I am that” is in reference to the Inner Controller (Antaryamin). “I am that, considering the Inner Controller, the Lord of lords.” As stated in the Mahakaurma: “All words are used even when there is a difference in the objects.” ॥ 13 ॥
